content:
In recent years, Mac has become increasingly accessible. With lower starting prices, more memory and storage per dollar, and the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple has, for the first time, become one of the best-value options on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple has raised prices significantly due to ongoing memory shortages. Macs are no longer as attractive as they were a few weeks ago, but that said, there are still some decent deals out there—if you need a new computer, I'd still say Macs currently offer good value compared to other computer products.

MacBook Air

Before the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry-level choice in Apple's laptop lineup. While the MacBook Neo has made its value proposition a little awkward, if you want a better user experience without needing top-tier specs, I still think the MacBook Air is an excellent laptop.

MagSafe, P3 wide colour gamut display, Center Stage for the webcam, and longer battery life are just some of the MacBook Air's highlights. It also comes in a 15-inch version, whereas the MacBook Neo is only available in 13 inches.

Currently, the entire MacBook Air lineup is available with the following discounts:

  • Refurbished M5 MacBook Air: 1TB storage, 16GB memory – $1,529 at the Apple Store

MacBook Neo

This product needs little introduction—the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, priced at just $699.

Compared to the MacBook Air mentioned above, there are indeed some trade-offs, but at this price point, it remains extremely attractive. Build quality, display clarity, and the macOS experience are essentially uncompromised. Of course, you'll have to accept a slower A18 Pro chip (though honestly, it's not weak at all), fewer ports, and only 8GB of memory, but at this price, that's entirely reasonable. It also comes in several eye-catching colour options, including citrus yellow, berry pink, and indigo.

The MacBook Neo currently has no notable retail discounts, but Apple offers refurbished versions that are $100 to $120 cheaper than retail. Apple refurbished products come with the same 1-year warranty and a nearly-new experience, with every major component replaced, so there are absolutely no scratches or battery degradation issues.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory – $689 on Amazon ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID – $789 on Amazon ($10 off)
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory – $599 at the Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID – $679 at the Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro sits at the top of the product lineup. You get access to the most cutting-edge specs, but there's one important caveat. Apple is reportedly set to redesign the higher-end MacBook Pro models later this year, introducing an OLED touchscreen and a thinner chassis.

However, that redesign will only come to models equipped with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—so if you're buying the base model with an M5 chip, there's absolutely no problem with buying a new one now. The same applies if you don't mind the new design at all, because the M5 Pro and M5 Max are still extremely impressive new chips.
